issues.description: Checkpoint save cadence is broken: save_interval is used as the train() length, but checkpoints save unconditionally each outer iteration
issues.detail: run() calls self.train() with iterator length=self.save_interval, then unconditionally saves a checkpoint after every train() return. There is no save_interval check and no per-step gating. If train() exits early (e.g. data exhausted before save_interval steps), or if save_interval does not divide max_step, the global_step in the checkpoint directory name will not match the documented 'Steps between checkpoints' contract. The invariant 'a checkpoint exists at every multiple of save_interval and only there' is not maintained. State the invariant explicitly and enforce it, or rename the field.

issues.description: trainer_args key mismatch between docstring and code: 'max_steps'/'val_interval' documented, 'max_step' read; val_interval never used
issues.detail: The __init__ docstring promises keys max_steps, log_interval, val_interval, save_interval, but the code reads trainer_args['max_step'] (singular) and never reads val_interval at all. log_interval is read but never used in train()/valid(). This is the kind of silent contract drift Knuth flags: a careful reader cannot tell from the code what the configuration schema actually is. Either the docstring is wrong or the code is; pick one and make them agree, and delete unused keys.

issues.description: all_reduce on stats requires every rank to send identical key sets in identical order; not enforced
issues.detail: _all_reduce_stats iterates `for key in stats` and issues collective ops per key. Collective communication requires every rank to call the same collectives in the same order with the same shapes. If different ranks ever produce different stats dicts (e.g. an optional metric only emitted when a batch contains a particular task type, or dict ordering drift), this will deadlock or corrupt. Either state and enforce the invariant 'stats has identical keys in identical order on every rank' (sort keys, validate length via a small all_reduce), or pack stats into a single fixed-shape tensor and reduce once. The current code is asymptotically fine but practically fragile.

issues.description: Validation averaging weights each batch equally regardless of batch size
issues.detail: valid() accumulates per-batch scalar stats into lists and reports sum(values)/len(values). For variable-size batches (which is the usual case in SpeechLM where collate_fn pads to the longest sequence and batchfy is length-bucketed), this is a batch-weighted average, not a sample-weighted average. The metric reported as 'val/<name>/loss' will silently disagree with what readers expect. Either document the invariant 'we report the mean over batches, assuming uniform batch size' or accumulate weighted by a count (n_tokens or n_samples) that the model returns alongside stats.

issues.description: Checkpoint discovery sort assumes a strict 'step_<int>' suffix; substring match accepts malformed dirs
issues.detail: _load_checkpoint filters checkpoints with `'step_' in d.name` (substring), then sorts by `int(x.name.split('step_')[-1])`. A directory named 'broken_step_abc' would pass the filter and crash the int() conversion; a directory named 'step_5_backup' would parse as 5_backup and also crash. The intended invariant is 'directory name matches exactly step_<positive int>'. Use a regex anchor, or startswith('step_') plus a try/except that skips non-conforming entries, and state the invariant in a comment.

issues.description: Valid/train specifier parsing uses split() rather than a documented separator; silent surprise with paths containing whitespace
issues.detail: train.py parses args.valid_unregistered_specifier.split() and args.valid_registered_specifier.split() to get a list of specs, but the argparse help text documents the format as 'task:name:data_json[:factor]' with no mention that multiple specs are whitespace-separated. A reader of train.py cannot tell from the help text how to pass two validation sets; a path containing a space will be silently split. Either document the separator in --help, or accept nargs='+' / a JSON list. Same applies to the registered variant.

issues.description: torch.cuda.set_device(args.local_rank) precedes argparse validation that local_rank is set
issues.detail: args.local_rank has default=None; if the launcher does not pass --local_rank (e.g. an older deepspeed launcher or a misconfigured invocation), torch.cuda.set_device(None) will raise an opaque TypeError before any logging is configured, making the failure hard to diagnose. State and check the invariant 'local_rank is a non-negative int < device_count' before touching CUDA, and emit a clear error if violated.

issues.description: train_dtype: 'amp' branch returns bf16/fp16 based on hw support, but pytorch AMP uses autocast at module level, not input casting
issues.detail: When amp is enabled, the code returns bfloat16 or float16 and to_device casts inputs to that dtype. PyTorch AMP (and DeepSpeed's amp) expects model inputs to remain float32; autocast handles per-op precision. Casting inputs to fp16 under amp will at minimum bypass amp's intended semantics and at worst cause dtype-mismatch errors inside the model. Either document why this code intentionally casts under amp, or only cast under fp16/bf16 modes where DeepSpeed expects fp16/bf16 inputs.

issues.description: No termination/progress audit: run() loop can spin forever if train() never advances global_step
issues.detail: The outer 'while self.global_step < self.max_step' loop relies on train() advancing global_step. If the train iterator yields zero batches (empty dataset for this rank's shard, exhausted state file, etc.), train() returns immediately without incrementing, valid() runs, a checkpoint is written, and we loop forever writing duplicate checkpoints at the same step. State the termination invariant ('each outer iteration advances global_step by at least 1') and assert it, or break on no progress.

issues.description: Missing literate comment on _all_reduce_stats: the async-then-wait pattern and its preconditions are non-obvious
issues.detail: The function uses async_op=True and gathers handles for efficiency, then divides by world_size to compute a mean. This is a small but real algorithmic choice that the reader has to reverse-engineer. A two-line comment stating: (1) preconditions (identical key set across ranks, tensors on the same device, sum semantics), (2) the rationale (overlap latency across keys), and (3) the postcondition (stats now holds rank-mean values) would make it readable without running.

issues.description: wandb.log uses step=self.global_step inside train(), but step is incremented after log; first log goes to step 0 twice on resume
issues.detail: In train(), wandb.log(stats, step=self.global_step) runs before self.global_step += 1. On resume, the first logged step equals the resumed global_step, which is also the last step logged before the checkpoint was saved. wandb may emit warnings or drop the duplicate. Either log at step+1 to match 'completed step', or document that step indexes the step about to complete.

issues.description: Mixed kebab-case and snake_case CLI flags (--train-config vs --local_rank, --resume_path) hurts readability
issues.detail: The argparse interface mixes --train-config, --output-dir (kebab) with --local_rank, --resume_path (snake). Argparse normalizes both to attribute names with underscores, so the code works, but a careful reader of the CLI surface sees inconsistency that suggests no one owns the interface design. Pick one convention and apply it; --local_rank is fixed by the deepspeed launcher convention, the rest should match it (snake) or be documented as 'launcher-imposed exception'.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED with a couple of NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT issues. The training loop is roughly correct in shape but several invariants are unstated and a few are actually wrong: save_interval is conflated with the inner train() length and checkpoints are written unconditionally; the trainer_args contract in the docstring (max_steps, val_interval, log_interval) disagrees with what the code reads (max_step) or never uses (val_interval, log_interval). The all_reduce-over-stats pattern is asymptotically fine but assumes identical key ordering on every rank without enforcing it, which is the kind of collective-comm landmine that deadlocks at 3am. Validation averaging is batch-weighted rather than sample-weighted with no comment saying so. None of these require a redesign; they require stating the invariants, fixing the contract drift, and adding a literate-grade comment to _all_reduce_stats and the run() loop.
